Reading Review — Jadviga Reduta

A2 Key for Schools — every wrong question, with the original text and why the correct answer is right.

                                      Part  Score                                       Wrong
1 — short notices                             5/6  Q5
2 — three texts, matching                     5/7  Q9, Q11
3 — long article                              2/5  Q14, Q15, Q16
4 — word-choice cloze                         1/6  Q19, Q20, Q21, Q22, Q23
5 — open cloze                                5/6  Q25

Part 1 — notices

  Q5 What should Andy do? — "I'm playing football with Tom this afternoon... Do you want to come too? Let me know. — Jake"
  A. invite friends to play football B. tell Jake if he can join him later ✓ C. show Tom where Woodside School is
  Why B: the message's real purpose is Jake's invitation + "Let me know" — that needs a reply. "Woodside School" is just background
  detail, not something Andy is asked to do.

Part 2 — three texts (Amy / Flora / Louisa), garden competition

Amy: "won a prize... flowers all different colours" · Flora: "won second prize... our prize is a visit to a special garden with butterflies" · Louisa: "flowers all
yellow... teacher taught us about the butterflies"

  Q9 Whose class won a trip? chosen: A Amy correct: B Flora ✓
  Why Flora: Amy won a prize too (TV film), but only Flora's prize is specifically a visit/trip ("a visit to a special garden").

  Q11 Whose class learnt about the insects? chosen: B Flora correct: C Louisa ✓
  Why Louisa: Flora's butterflies are only where her prize trip goes — she didn't learn about them. Louisa says "our teacher taught us"
  about the butterflies — that's actual learning.

Part 3 — "Starting at a new school" (Anna Gray, 11)

  Q14 How did Anna feel about moving? — "I was excited to move to a new school"
  chosen: A worried about older children correct: B happy about doing something different ✓
  Why B: the text's exact word is "excited", not worried — A is invented, nothing in the text supports it.

  Q15 Who is Anna's best friend now? — "I started talking to the girl who was sitting beside me in maths. She lives near me..."
  chosen: B someone from her home area correct: C someone she met in her new class ✓
  Why C: "she lives near me" comes after they'd already met in class — that's how Anna found out, not why they became friends. Classic
  wrong-order trap.

  Q16 What does Anna say about the timetable? — "there were lots of subjects, some were quite new to me"
  chosen: C difficult to understand correct: A includes subjects she didn't do before ✓
  Why A: "new to me" describes the subjects, not the timetable being confusing — "difficult" in the text refers to lessons being harder, a
  different idea.

Part 4 — "Wivenhoe hotel" word-choice cloze (5 of 6 wrong)

  Q19 "a big ___ between Wivenhoe and other hotels" chosen: B variety correct: C difference ✓ — "difference between" is fixed;
  "variety" needs of/in, not between.

  Q20 "young people who are ___ to get jobs" chosen: C explaining correct: B hoping ✓ — "hoping to get a job" is natural; "explaining
  to get" isn't grammatical.

  Q21 "jobs in the hotel or restaurant ___" chosen: C career correct: B work ✓ — "hotel or restaurant work" is the set phrase; "career"
  needs its own article to sound right.

  Q22 "their teachers ___ them carefully" chosen: A see correct: C watch ✓ — "watch carefully" = supervise; "see carefully" isn't
  idiomatic.

  Q23 "preparing menus and ___ the telephone" chosen: A calling correct: B answering ✓ — "answer the telephone" is fixed; you call
  a person, not the phone.

Part 5 — open cloze (email)

  Q25 "I'm glad that you like ___ new house" written: A correct: your / the ✓
  Why "your": it's a specific, already-known house (the friend's own new house) — "a" is for something never mentioned before.

Pattern: in Parts 2–3 Jadviga picks the option that reuses a real word from the text but attaches it to the wrong person or the wrong cause/
effect (Q9, Q11, Q15). In Part 4 she picks the closest general meaning but breaks the fixed collocation the gap needs (difference between,
hoping to, watch carefully, answer the phone) — a vocabulary-in-context issue, not comprehension. Practice: "who said this exactly, and why"
drills for Part 2/3; verb/noun + preposition collocations for Part 4.
